Resubmitted with the deterministic gap repaired in operative language.

**What changed from the first submission:** the verifier's mechanical miss — no stated warranty period — is now cured inside the same single inserted subsection rather than being argued away in the rationale. § 16.1(G) now reads as "Warranty Period; Remedy" and does two things:

1. **Express period at the fallback floors** — "shall remain in effect throughout the Term and in any event for not less than ninety (90) days following delivery of each report and thirty (30) days following performance of each Service." Phrasing it as a floor ("in any event for not less than") on top of "throughout the Term" means we gain a confirmable numeric period without converting the existing untimed, continuing warranties into sunsetting ones. I deliberately did not volunteer the preferred 12-month software period, since 90/30 are the selected fallback thresholds.
2. **Remedy** — repair or replacement, or at Customer's election a refund of the fees paid, unchanged from the validated first draft.

**Coverage:** all four fallback elements are now `addressed_by_operation` on operation 1; no `already_met` claims remain, so there is no reliance on an inferred duration.

**Preserved:** the favourable § 16.1(F) carve-back, the § 12.3 non-exclusive remedies, and every existing word of A–F are untouched — the change is purely additive and lettered (G.) to sit cleanly in the A–F sequence. "Term" is a defined term (§ 1(X)), so no dangling reference. No survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories, or procedure was added; the preferred-only items remain rationale notes rather than smuggled-in terms.
